raw_response.headline_result_summary: Across 2,119 US municipally owned and operated drinking water systems (serving cities >= 10,000 residents), monthly household bills for basic drinking water services (6,000 gal/month; mean $38.60, range $5.00-$163.40) show mixed associations with institutional, organizational, fiscal, regulatory, and governance factors in the primary state-fixed-effects Combined OLS model (Table 3, Column 5). Specifically: (1) Mayor vs. council-manager/other form of government is statistically null in the Combined model (b = -1.03, SE = 0.76), attenuating from a negative association in the partial Organizational model (Col 3: b = -1.58**, SE = 0.69, p < 0.05); (2) municipal government size (FTEs per capita: b = 0.026, SE = 0.072) and past 5-year SDWA health-based regulatory violations (b = 0.96, SE = 0.86) are also statistically null in the Combined model; (3) wholesale purchased water dependence (b = 2.86**, SE = 0.91, p < 0.05) and per-capita water utility expenditures (b = 0.0055***, SE = 0.00080, p < 0.01; plus municipal debt ratio b = 0.40*, SE = 0.24, p < 0.10) are associated with higher household water bills (worse direct price affordability, though reflecting higher infrastructure investment or wholesale compliance capacity); and (4) larger municipal population scale (b = -2.08***, SE = 0.41, p < 0.01; 25% lower cost in largest vs. smallest cities, highlighting economies of scale over fragmented decentralization) and more conservative resident ideology (b = -5.44**, SE = 2.41, p < 0.05; 18% lower cost than liberal cities) are associated with lower monthly household water bills.
raw_response.specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. Outcome polarity and interpretation: The dependent variable Water cost is the nominal monthly household water bill in dollars for 6,000 gal (higher = MORE expensive / WORSE direct price affordability, NOT better access). Furthermore, the authors caution (pp. 2, 9) that they measure household cost rather than income-adjusted affordability and that lower bills (e.g., in conservative or higher-% Hispanic cities) may reflect infrastructure underinvestment rather than favorable affordability policy. 2. Restricted ownership sample: All 2,119 utilities are municipally owned and operated systems in cities >= 10,000 population; private utilities and special districts are excluded, so public vs. private ownership is not tested. 3. Block-to-Combined attenuation: Form of government (1 = Mayor) is significant in the partial Organization model (Table 3 Col 3: -1.58**, p < 0.05) and borderline in EPA-region FE Col 3 (-1.903*, p < 0.10), but is null (-1.03, SE = 0.76) in the primary Combined model (Table 3 Col 5). Government size similarly drops from 0.090* (p < 0.10) to null (0.026, SE = 0.072). Conversely, Debt ratio is null in Col 1 (0.29, SE = 0.22), borderline p < 0.10 in Col 5 (0.40*, SE = 0.24), and p < 0.05 in Appendix Tables A1 and A2. 4. Published table mislabeling/typos: (a) In Appendix Table A1, Democratic presidential vote share replaces conservative ideology (flipped scale), yet the row is still mislabeled 'Conservative ideology' (b = +14.22** vs. -5.44** in Table 3); (b) Surface water (1 = surface, 0 = ground) has a garbled description in Table 2 and is mislabeled 'GW' in Tables A1 and A2 (b = +5.299*** and +6.242***); (c) In Table 3 Col 5, Median income is printed as '-0.066 (0.023)' without stars while the text (p. 7) and Figure 3 confirm a null relationship (likely a typo for -0.0066), and Monthly moisture is printed as '4.11 (1.70)' without stars.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional observational study using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) linear regression with state fixed effects (and sensitivity models with EPA 10-region fixed effects) and state-clustered robust standard errors
raw_response.unit_and_sample_size: US municipalities (population >= 10,000 in the contiguous United States) with municipally owned and operated drinking water systems; rate data collected for 2,161 municipalities, primary analytic sample n = 2,119 municipalities (n = 2,003 in Appendix Table A1 sensitivity analysis)
